title: Solver-reconciliation gate over the real anomalies
purpose: S5 reports; G2 asserts what it reports on the real projects and pins the interpretation, so a later change cannot quietly reclassify the two known anomalies.

A.why: no owner slot recorded, so nothing can be proven about it

B.why: a later job succeeded in the same owner slot (revision 3 > 2)

the_two_anomalies.central_claim: they agree on execution and evidence and differ only in relevance - which is exactly why one flag could not answer for both

gate_assertions: both anomalies report deterministic execution from the exit artifact while the db row stays stale
neither has COMPLETE evidence, because no completion receipt exists
A blocks with UNRESOLVED; B does not block, being provably SUPERSEDED
A has exactly two blockers, both UNRESOLVED
B and R have no blockers at all
reading a real project mutates nothing - revision, event count, job count, file size and even mtime are unchanged
the six relevance values are a closed set and the blocking pair is REQUIRED + UNRESOLVED
the result is JSON-serialisable, since S5 is a shadow evaluator that must be reportable

test_baseline.note: the real-project evaluations make this gate take ~29s; that is accepted because it is the only place the anomalies are asserted against real data
